pr.title: Stop the keychain mock patch before starting it again
pr.head: a7ce1ec6229d50fd830d0daf4515a9b26ed40db5

summary: The Linux keychain test checks that project agent key init stores its secret through standard input and leaves configuration untouched when the keychain fails. A reused mock patch made that test error on newer Python releases before it could finish those checks.

Each simulated keychain call now runs inside a fresh patch context. The missing-tool case keeps the fixture’s absent path, and the existing success and failure assertions stay in place. Production code is unchanged.

groups.title: Keep each keychain scenario isolated
groups.kicker: A fresh patch for each simulated backend call
intro: A mock patch temporarily replaces SECRET_TOOL, the path used to launch Linux’s keychain program. The fixture normally points that path at a file that does not exist, so the test can exercise a machine without the program.

The helper creates a new patch each time the fake program is needed. Its context restores the fixture’s path after success or an exception. A null context leaves that path alone for the missing-program scenario.

files.note: The Linux backend test scopes each fake keychain invocation and preserves its storage and failure checks.

checks.text: The merge-base test fails on Python 3.15.2 with “Patch is already started”; all 57 relay tests pass at this head on Python 3.15.2 and Python 3.12.5.

Fixture setup gives SECRET_TOOL an absent path. The missing mode leaves that value intact, while the fail and hang modes use fresh patch contexts; the existing outcomes assertion checks refusal and absence of saved configuration.
